headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.46 (95% CI: 0.31–0.69), suggesting that omega-6 fatty acids is associated with a lower risk of bladder cancer. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.

sample_size.excerpt: Dietary data were collected from 322 cases and 239 controls, and OR and 95 % CI were calculated using unconditional logistic regression.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 322 + 239 = 561

cases.excerpt: Dietary data were collected from 322 cases and 239 controls, and OR and 95 % CI were calculated using unconditional logistic regression.

effect_size.excerpt: Borderline statistically significant reduced odds were detected for polyunsaturated fat (OR 0·43, 95 % CI 0·19, 0·98; P for trend = 0·07) and linoleic acid (OR 0·43, 95 % CI 0·19, 0·96; P for trend = 0·06). These fats and fatty acids were highly correlated and following adjustment for each other, the only potential inverse association to remain was for ALA.
